_si: SI-assisted: script written with Claude Code (Anthropic); inputs copied from the cited sources.
label: arithmetic from measured half-lives, not a field measurement
model: single exponential (first-order) decay: straw(t) = initial_t_ha * 2 ** (-(days since management) / half_life_days)
how_to_read: straw_t_ha_low = lowest initial straw managed at the start of the window (oldest straw); straw_t_ha_high = highest initial straw managed on the latest date that is still before the target. Fields whose management date falls after the target are not counted (their crop is still standing).

rotations.label: Soybean - wheat (wheat straw left at harvest)

initial_sources.low: F11 (3.0 t/ha wheat straw, Roman 1990, cited in Santos et al. 2019)
initial_sources.high: F11 (wheat residue remaining 3.82-4.12 t/ha, Coxilha RS, 1995-2002, Santos et al. 2019)

rotations.window_source: Scenario from the team brief (wheat harvest October-November). Context, Rio Grande do Sul state: 42% of the wheat area harvested on 6 Nov 2025 against a 5-season average of 64% for the same date, and harvest practically over on 11 Dec 2025 (Emater/RS Informativo Conjuntural, as reported by Revista Cultivar, refs E1 and E2). No Cruz Alta harvest calendar was found.

rotations.label: Soybean - cover crop (black oat, desiccated)

initial_sources.low: F9 (black oat 4,390 kg dry matter/ha, Santa Maria RS, Aita & Giacomini 2003)
initial_sources.high: F11 (black oat straw 8.2 t/ha, Roman 1990, cited in Santos et al. 2019)

rotations.window_source: Scenario from the team brief (desiccation September-October). No published desiccation calendar for Cruz Alta was found in this session.

rotations.label: Soybean - winter fallow
rotations.window_source: Soybean residue from the previous April harvest is not modelled: the trial reports no soybean half-life.

limitations: The half-lives come from one long-term trial (Cruz Alta, no-till, Campos et al. 2011b); decomposition changes with rain, temperature and residue placement, so another year or field can differ.
A single exponential is assumed; the trial reports half-lives, and the curve shape between the measurements is not tested here.
The initial straw values come from other sites (Santa Maria, Coxilha, and Roman 1990 as cited by Embrapa), not from Cruz Alta fields.
No source here converts straw (t/ha) into the share of soil covered, so how much straw is enough is not given.
The management windows are scenarios from the team brief, not observed dates.
